image_description: A close-up, side-profile view of a dark-colored turtle, likely a mud or musk turtle, resting on a mossy rock. The turtle has a high-domed, textured carapace that appears rough and possibly algae-covered. One front limb is visible, showing webbed toes and claws. The head is partially visible with a small eye and pointed snout. The background is blurred green foliage.

The claws on the visible foot appear slightly fused and lack distinct, sharp separation from the toe pads. They look somewhat melted into the substrate.
The eye appears slightly flat and painted-on, lacking the depth and reflective quality of a real reptile eye, though this is subtle.
